subject: nlm code 5 and Inf. for sigma SE

messages.author: b85d22558143e510
messages.subject: nlm code 5 and Inf. for sigma SE
parts:
Hi - 

I am getting an error message I've never had before and am hoping someone can provide some insight.  

I am attempting to run the following model:
D~1,g0~1,sigma~buff10_tri

buff10_tri is a covariate for terrain ruggedness.  

I am getting the following error message: 
Warning message: In secr.fit(CHmale2006S, model = list(D ~ 1, g0 ~ buff169_rdens,  : possible maximization error: nlm returned code 5. See ?nlm

Most, but not all, models with terrain ruggedness as a covariate on sigma produce this error.  I was able to resolve the error message by scaling the covariate and using starting values.  However, I am now getting nonsensical estimates of sigma: 

       link     estimate  SE.estimate          lcl          ucl
D       log 7.333878e-06 2.847482e-06 3.518630e-06 1.528599e-05
g0    logit 1.269357e-02 4.418127e-03 6.401242e-03 2.501543e-02
sigma   log 3.242634e+14          Inf 0.000000e+00          Inf

I suspect the issue might have to do with the sparse data, which includes 16 detections of 9 individuals.  When I run the same models on the female data set which is 22 detections of 9 individuals, I do not have any issues. 

Any suggestions?

Thanks!
Andrea

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: nlm code 5 and Inf. for sigma SE
parts:
There's every sign that the model is not identifiable with the particular data you have, so yes, it has to do with sparse data. This happens.
Murray

messages.author: b1d2e118c1689e57
messages.subject: RE: nlm code 5 and Inf. for sigma SE
parts:
Hi Andrea,

 

As a rule of thumb I would ask ‘would I do a regression with these data’, and for only 9 individuals..no I would not do a regression, so indeed these are very sparse data.

 

I did wonder why you weren’t combining males and females in one analysis (doubling your sample size). You could then fit effects for sex on g0 and sigma, and if they were not significant, gain some statistical power from the pooling for investigating other covariates.

 

Regards,

   James

Thanks
Andrea
